tagline: A dam builders' wagon road, still dirt where the mountains are steepest.
intro: SR 88 leaves Apache Junction for the Superstition Mountains on a road first cut in 1904 to haul supplies to the Roosevelt Dam site. It passes Canyon Lake and Tortilla Flat on pavement, then turns to dirt and follows the Salt River the rest of the way to the dam.
It was one of Arizona's ten original state highways in 1927, and most of the stretch between Fish Creek Bridge and Roosevelt Lake has never been paved.

moments.title: Canyon Lake
moments.text: The smallest of the four reservoirs on the Salt River, held back since 1925 by Mormon Flat Dam.

moments.title: Tortilla Flat
moments.text: The last surviving stagecoach stop on the Apache Trail, and by the Post Office's reckoning Arizona's smallest community with its own post office and voting precinct.

moments.title: Theodore Roosevelt Dam
moments.text: The reason for the road: a 357-foot dam built between 1905 and 1911 that holds back the Salt River as Roosevelt Lake.

practical: Past Tortilla Flat the road is unpaved, narrow and winding. The stretch between mileposts 222 and 229 was closed after the 2019 Woodbury Fire and floods, and reopened in September 2024.
